newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: COMMBANK SHARES DIP EARLY, BOUNCE OFF LOWS.
newsitem.headline: COMMBANK SHARES DIP EARLY, BOUNCE OFF LOWS.

text.p: Shares in Commonwealth Bank of Australia slid to A$16.02 in early trade, its lowest level in more than a month following the release of its full year profit.
However, by 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT) the shares had regained some ground to be down 22 cents at A$16.15, broadly in line with the sector and an overall weaker market.
The bank reported a net profit for the year to June 30 of A$1.08 billion and announced a final dividend of 57 cents per share, bringing the annual payout to A$1.02 per share.
An abnormal loss of A$200 million, related to restructuring in its information technology unit, weighed on the result.

"On the face of it they are under the same local pressure as NAB," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank, noting previous warnings on domestic margins by sector leader, National Australia Bank.
However, the dealer said general weakness in the broader market following Wall Street's fall made an accurate reflection of the results difficult to gauge.
"The market is down anyway and that makes it a bit difficult to tell the real impact. The analysts will still be looking at the numbers and that will take a while to digest."

The bank also announced a share buyback of A$650 million, due to occur around the end of 1997, and a partnership with U.S.-based Electronic Data Systems (EDS) that sees CommBank take a 35 percent stake in EDS's Australian unit.
The alliance is due to last at least 10 years and is expected to generate gross revenues of A$5 billion.

By 11.15 a.m. (0115 GMT), CommBank shares were 27 cents or 1.7 percent lower at A$16.10. NAB was down 1.8 percent at A$18.75, ANZ Bank lost 2.5 percent to A$9.71, while Westpac lost 1.9 percent to A$8.17.
